pattern: The user approved a self-contained Azure Commercial DEV/TEST MVP, Bicep rather than azd, with no deployment or tenant/subscription changes during implementation.
implication: Use resource-group-scope IaC, synthetic data, explicit operational exceptions, and record plan approval from the conversation. Do not invent existing Azure resources or claim live discovery.

pattern: Plaintext stays in the intended browser flow. Direct Entra bearer authentication is approved with DPoP replay risk accepted; file access and data entitlement are separate.
implication: Expose app and platform through HTTPS, configure the exact app CORS origin and tenant/API audience, use claims ERS and Files.User/Platform.Admin role mappings, and give only the file API identity container-scoped Blob access.

pattern: The pinned upstream service/v0.29.0 supports standard exportable RSA/EC PEM cryptography and PostgreSQL; no built-in Azure Key Vault KAS crypto driver was verified.
implication: Persist generated KAS keys and origin-specific YAML as Container Apps secrets, use private PostgreSQL with password authentication and verified TLS, and document backup, rotation, migration, and privileged-runtime limitations.

pattern: Container Apps default domains exist only after environment provisioning, while OpenTDF CORS and browser configuration need stable endpoint names.
implication: Deploy foundation first, derive URLs from stable app names plus environment.defaultDomain, then generate a secure runtime parameter file and deploy apps. Retain names and the same password/keys across stages.

pattern: The approved architecture requires private Blob Storage and PostgreSQL, and an image registry. Shared Docker services are unavailable and must not be started.
implication: Use a workload-profiles consumption environment on a delegated /24 subnet, separate delegated PostgreSQL and endpoint subnets, and Premium private ACR. Require a separately provided VNet-connected build/push runner; do not create an unused runner or claim local image execution.
